PE40: (O Prabhu!) Where no other (being is able to help), there, O Prabhu, You alone are able to help.
Where You are, Almighty Lord, there is no one else.
There You are, O Omnipotent Lord, where there is none else.
O Capable One! Where there is no protector, there You alone are the protector.
God, where nobody else is capable of helping, You alone can.
8NMU: Rakh = protection, support. Udar agni = the fire of (the mother's) belly.
In the fire of the mother's womb it is Your support alone that the being has.
There, in the fire of the mother's womb, You protected us.
There in the fire of mother's womb, You protectest the mortal, O Lord.
In the fire that is within the belly, there too is Your protection alone.
There is your protection, even in the fire (warmth) of the mother's womb.
MNNT: (O Prabhu! Hearing Your Nam) the jamduts (do not come near); by the grace of Your Nam they leave (the being) and go away.
Hearing Your Name, the Messenger of Death runs away.
Hearing Your Name, the Death's couriers leave off the Mortal.
Hearing Your Nam the messengers of the Jam too leave and go.
On hearing of Your Name God, the Messenger of Death leaves us alone.
7HQ7: Bikhamu = hard. Asgahu = very deep, whose bottom cannot be reached. Pari pahi = they cross over.
This hard and fathomless world-ocean the beings cross over with (the help of) the Guru's shabad.
The terrifying, treacherous, impassible world-ocean is crossed over, through the Word of the Guru's Shabad.
The dreadful, formidable and unfathomable world-ocean is crossed through the Guru's instruction.
That world-ocean which is unfathomable and bottomless, and hard to cross — its far shore is reached by the Guru's updesh.
Y2CL: Sei = those men alone. Amritu = the Nam-water that gives spiritual life. Khahi = they eat, they drink.
But those men alone drink the Nam-water that gives spiritual life within whom the hunger and thirst for it has arisen.
Those who feel thirst for You, take in Your Ambrosial Nectar.
They, who feel thirst for You partake of Your Nectar.
Those persons in whom the thirst which is faith has arisen, they alone eat the fruit of the Nam-amrit.
Only those who feel the thirst for the spiritual life are able to consume this Amrit (nectar of Naam that gives spiritual life).
2W6U: Kali = the world. Punn = virtuous act. Gahi = they sing.
(Those) who, holding the simran of the Nam to be the best and most virtuous act in the world, sing the virtues of Prabhu.
This is the only act of goodness in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga, to sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord of the Universe.
This is the only virtuous deed in the Darkage, that one sings the praise of the World-Lord.
In Kalyug the singing of the virtues of Gobind — this alone is the great merit.
In this dark world, the highest good is to sing of God's virtues.
RXFG: Sabhsai no = to every being. Sahi sahi = in every breath.
The merciful Prabhu takes care of every being with every breath.
He is Merciful to all; He sustains us with each and every breath.
The Master is merciful to all. He takes care of everyone at every breath.
O Merciful One! You take care of everyone breath by breath — the sense being, You sustain the beings at every moment.
CFFK: Birtha = empty. Tudhu ahi = Your shelter. Ji = whichever ||9||
O Prabhu! Whichever being comes to Your shelter goes not empty (from Your door). ||9||
Those who come to You with love and faith are never turned away empty-handed. ||9||
O Nanak, none who longingly comes to Yours door, O Lord, returns empty-handed.
Whoever comes desiring (tudhu) Your shelter, none goes empty — the sense being, he obtains dharam, arth, kam and moksh. ||9||
Nobody leaves empty-handed after longing for Your Sanctuary.

AQH2: Apar = a-par, whose far shore cannot be found. Martaba = rank.
O Prabhu! Your rank is endlessly great,
The greatest of the great, infinite is Your dignity.
The highest of the high and unrivalled is Your dignity, O Lord.
O Boundless One! Your rank is the greatest of the great.
N0UE: Rang parang = of many colours. Na japann = cannot be understood.
(in the world) countless kinds of Your wonders are taking place, which cannot be understood.
Your colors and hues are so numerous; no one can know Your actions.
Various are Yours colours and super-colours. Yours wondrous deeds, one can realise not.
You have made separate colours and (parang) mixed colours; countless are Your works, which cannot be known.
MLLU: Jiu = life, support. Janla = the knower.
Within all beings You alone are their life; You know everything (about beings).
You are the Soul within all souls; You alone know everything.
You alone are the inner life of the living beings and knowest everything.
Being the life within all beings, You know everything.
GHA4: Vas = in the power. Bhala = beautiful.
Beautiful is Your dwelling; the whole creation is in Your power alone.
Everything is under Your control; Your home is beautiful.
Everything is under Your sway and beauteous is Your mansion.
Everything is in Your power; Your home — Vaikunth, or the sat sangat — is good.
UJVA: Ghar = in the home. Tudh ghar = in Your home. Vadhai = rejoicing, celebrations.
(Even as master of so vast a creation,) in Your heart there is always bliss and rejoicing,
Your home is filled with bliss, which resonates and resounds throughout Your home.
In Your home there is bliss and it is Your home in which congratulations ever pour in.
In Your home, the sat sangat, there is always rejoicing and bliss.
Z7CD: Mahta = greatness. Tej = glory. Jar = You bear.
You Yourself bear Your own so great honour, greatness and glory.
Your honor, majesty and glory are Yours alone.
Yours celebrity, magnificence and glory behoove You alone.
The (man) honour, (mahta) greatness and radiance that are Your own — You Yourself bear them.
61YS: Kala = power, strength. Jat kata = everywhere.
The Master-Prabhu of all powers is seen everywhere.
You are overflowing with all powers; wherever we look, there You are.
You are brimful with all the potencies and are seen everywhere.
Full of every power, You are seen wherever one looks.
2TPP: Dasan das = servant of the servants. ||18||
O Prabhu! Nanak, the servant of Your servants, prays before You (alone). ||18||
Nanak, the slave of Your slaves, prays to You alone. ||18||
Nanak, the slave of Your salves, O Lord, makes supplication before You.
Sri Guru ji says: may I be the servant of Your servants — this I (binvata) say before You. ||18||

U2FL: Rai Balvand = by Rai Balvand. Tatha = and. Satai = by Satta. Doom = by the doom, the minstrel, the rababi. Satai doom = by Satta the rababi. Aakhi = uttered, recited.
This is the 'Var' in Raamkali that Rai Balvand and Satta the minstrel recited.
Vaar Of Raamkalee, Uttered By Satta And Balwand The Drummer:
Var of Ramkali. Uttered by Rai Balwand and Satta, the drummer.
0MBD: Akal Purakh is one, and is met by the Satguru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God, By True Guru's grace, He is obtained.
J48F: Nau = name, renown, honour, greatness. Bol = word, speech. Jokhivdai = to weigh, for (that renown) to be weighed, measured. Kiu hovai = how can it be? It cannot.
The renown that the Almighty Creator Himself makes (high) — no word (from anyone) can weigh it (that is, who am I, poor Balvand, to describe the Guru's high station?).
One who chants the Name of the Almighty Creator - how can his words be judged?
How can the words of him, who utters the Name of the omnipotent Creator be weighed?

Guru Nanak ji, whose name the Almighty has made (equal to) the Creator — that is, made equal to Himself; or, the one whose name the all-powerful Parmeshvar makes great — how can his words be (jokhivdai) weighed? Or how can he be weighed with words? Or how can his words be (khivdai) borne? Or how could they ever wear out?
LA5E: De guna sat = divine qualities like truth. Parangat = the spiritual state that can carry one across. Dan = gift. Parhivdai = to obtain.

The divine qualities like truth (that people labour to build within themselves) to obtain the gift of the spiritual state that carries one across the world-ocean — (for the Satguru these qualities) are his sisters and brothers (that is, they are naturally present in him).
His divine virtues are the true sisters and brothers; through them, the gift of supreme status is obtained.
The angelic virtues are the true sisters and brothers Through them the gift of salvation is obtained.

The divine qualities such as truth are his brothers, and compassion, friendliness, gladness and equanimity are his sisters. (Parangat dan) From such a Satguru the Sikhs (parhivdai) receive the gift of liberation.
J7PW: Nanak = by Nanak. Kot = fortress. Satani = strong. Neev = foundation. Dai = laying.
Guru Nanak Dev ji (of such high renown) established the rule (of dharma), building the fortress of truth and laying a strong foundation.
Nanak established the kingdom; He built the true fortress on the strongest foundations.
Nanak established the Lord's empire and laid a very strong foundation of the fortress of truth.

Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji has run such a rule: he made the fortress of the true Name, and (satani) with strength gave faith and devotion; that is, for being established in one's own true form through (raj) light — that is, wisdom — he kept devotion foremost.
H34D: Dharion = he (Guru Nanak) placed. Lahne dharion chhat sir = he placed the canopy on Lahna's head. Kar sifti = through praise. Amrit pivdai = (on the head of Lahna ji) who was drinking the amrit of the Name.
Guru Nanak Dev ji placed the canopy (of Guruship) on the head of (Baba) Lahna ji, who, through praise, was drinking the water of the Name that gives spiritual life.
He installed the royal canopy over Lehna's head; chanting the Lord's Praises, He drank in the Ambrosial Nectar.
Nanak placed the Royal crown, over Angad's head and hymning Lord's praise, he quaffed Nectar.

Sri Guru Nanak ji placed the canopy of Guruship on Lahna's head; that is, made Lahna ji the teacher of wisdom. And what is Lahna ji like? One who, (sifti) praising Vahiguru, drinks the amrit of bliss.
VXN5: Mat gur atam dev di = through the wisdom of the Guru, the Divine Self. Atamdev = Akal Purakh. Kharhag = with the sword. Jor = with force. Parakui = with prowess, with strength. (Note: 'parakui' is the instrumental singular of 'parakau', the Prakrit form of Sanskrit 'prakram'.) Jia = the gift of life, spiritual life. Dai = giving. Amrit = the water of the Name, which gives spiritual life.
With the sword of wisdom (given by) the Guru, Akal Purakh, with force and with strength, (removing the old life within,) giving spiritual life,
The Guru implanted the almighty sword of the Teachings to illuminate his soul.
Guru Nanak placed the soul illuminating, supremely powerful sword of his instruction in Lahna's mind.
The teaching of Parmatma that the Guru gave is the labour; the (kharhag) double-edged sword is wisdom, and he gave Lahna ji a (jor) fine and (parakui) powerful one.
Q9PS: Gur = by the Guru, Guru Nanak Dev ji. Chele rahras = the salutation of the disciple (Baba Lahna ji). Rahras = prayer, salutation, obeisance. Kii = did. Gur Nanak = by Guru Nanak. Salamat thivdai = while still in good health, in his own lifetime, while physically alive.
(now) in his own lifetime Guru Nanak Dev ji bowed before his own Sikh (Baba Lahna ji),
The Guru bowed down to His disciple, while Nanak was still alive.
During his very life-time Guru Nanak made obeisance to Angad, his disciple.
The custom of Guru and disciple — Sri Guru Nanak ji (kii) carried it out (salamat thivdai) while still in his own body.
K09T: Sah = by the Master, the Guru. Ditos = gave, gave him. Jivdai = while alive. ||1||
and the Satguru gave (Baba Lahna ji) the tilak (of Guruship) while still alive. ||1||
The King, while still alive, applied the ceremonial mark to his forehead. ||1||
Guru Nanak, the King, while alive gave the apostolic mark to Angad.
The custom he carried out was this: the Master, Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji, gave Lahna ji the (tika) tilak of Guruship while he himself was still living. ||1||
NDDD: Lahne di = Lahna's (proclamation), the fame of Baba Lahna ji's greatness. Pherai-ai = spread, went round. Nanaka dohi khatiai = by the blessing of (Guru) Nanak's proclamation. Dohi = the fame of glory. Khatiai = through the earnings, by the blessing.
(When Guru Nanak Dev ji gave the tilak of Guruship to Baba Lahna ji, then) by the blessing of the fame of Guru Nanak Sahib's greatness, the fame of Baba Lahna ji's greatness spread;
Nanak proclaimed Lehna's succession - he earned it.
As the reward of his service, Nanak got announced the proclamation of Lahna's accession.
The proclamation of Lahna ji, sent round by Sri Guru Nanak ji, is (khatiai) being won.
KFDU: Sai = the same. Jugat = the way of living. Sah = by the Master (the Guru). Kaia = body.
because (within Baba Lahna ji) was the very same light (as Guru Nanak Sahib's), and the way of life too was the same; the Guru (Nanak Dev ji) had (only) changed the body.
They shared the One Light and the same way; the King just changed His body.
The same is the Divine light and same the life department. The king (Nanak)has again merely changed his body.
The light is the very one of Sri Guru Nanak ji, (jugat sai) and the order of discourse and kirtan is the same too; the Master, Sri Guru Nanak ji, has only changed to another body.
KFKD: Su chhat niranjani = the beautiful divine canopy. Mal = taking possession, holding. Gur hatiai = in the Guru's (Nanak's) shop, in Guru Nanak's house.
The beautiful divine canopy waves (over Baba Lahna's head). In Guru Nanak Dev ji's shop, (Baba Lahna) has taken the seat (to hand out the treasure of the 'Name' received from Guru Nanak Dev ji).
The immaculate canopy waves over Him, and He sits on the throne in the Guru's shop.
The beauteous Divine umbrella waves over him(Angad) and he has occupied Guru Nanak's shop and sits on his throne.
The canopy of the praise of the Pure One waves over his head. O Lahna ji! You have taken (gur hatiai) the throne of Guruship.
HZCK: Karah = (Baba Lahna ji) does. Gur furmaia = the order the Guru gave. Jog = the yoga of 'the Guru's order'. Sil aluni chatiai = (the yoga of carrying out the Guru's order is) like licking a saltless stone (very hard work).
(Baba Lahna ji) carries out the order given by Guru Nanak Sahib — earning this yoga of 'obeying the order' is like licking a saltless stone (very hard work).
He does as the Guru commands; He tasted the tasteless stone of Yoga.
He does that what Guru Nanak ordered him and tastes the insipid stone, leading to the union with the Lord.
(Ji) Whatever the Guru ordered, he obeyed that order, and received the yoga of devotion. He licks what is without the salt of worldly pleasure — that is, he takes its taste.

H1TW: Gur sabad = through the Satguru's Shabad. Aavi = comes. Har tot...khatiai = har khatiai tot na aavi, there is no loss in the earnings of Hari's Name. (Meaning:) at Baba Lahna ji's door the storehouse of the Name is being given out through the Satguru's Shabad, (and even after giving out so much) there is no shortfall in Baba Lahna ji's earnings of the Name.
(In Guru Nanak's shop) the langar (of the Name) runs through the Guru's Shabad, (yet in Baba Lahna ji's) earnings of the Name there is no shortfall.
The Langar - the Kitchen of the Guru's Shabad has been opened, and its supplies never run short.
The kitchen of the Guru's Divine word is opened and there occurs no deficiency in his earnings.
The langar runs, and, O Guru, words concerning Hari are spoken — that is, you are teaching how to reach Parmeshvar. You have earned wealth and powers that never run short — or have earned devotion.
6D5A: Kharche = spends, gives out. Dit khasamm di = the gift given by the Master (Akal Purakh). Aap khahdi = used (the gift of the Name) himself. Khair = in alms, in charity. Dabtiai = handed out in heaps.
(Baba Lahna ji) is giving out the gift of the Name given by Akal Purakh; he uses it himself and (also) gives it away in heaps (to others).
Whatever His Master gave, He spent; He distributed it all to be eaten.
He expends the Lord's gift himself, eats and copiously distributes the alms.
You spend the gift given by the Master, and (aap khahdi) eat it yourself — repeat the Name; and you (dabtiai) hand out charity — that is, you teach others.
X936: Noor = light. Aras = the sky, the heavens. Kuras = the disc of sun and moon. Arsahu kursahu = from the spiritual realm, from the land of the spirit. Jhatiai = is being showered, is falling abundantly.
(In Guru Angad Sahib's court) the praise of the Master, Akal Purakh, goes on; light is showering (at his door) from the realms of the spirit.
The Praises of the Master were sung, and the Divine Light descended from the heavens to the earth.
The Lord's praises are sung and Divine light descends from firmament and heavenly bodies.

The praise of (khasamm) Parmeshvar is going on in your court; the (noor) light of Vahiguru, whose throne is (kursahu) in (arsahu) Vaikunth, is (jhatiai) falling — that is, you have the glory of Vishnu ji.
JZ9J: Sache patisah = O true Satguru Angad Dev ji! Janam janam di = of many births.
O true Satguru (Angad Dev ji)! By seeing you, the filth (of vices) of many births is being cut away.
Gazing upon You, O True King, the filth of countless past lives is washed away.
Beholding you, O True King, the filth of births over births is washed off.
O True King! Just by seeing you, the filth of sin of birth after birth is cut away.
CYST: Gur = by the Guru (Nanak). Edu = from this. Edu bolahu = from this word, from the word given by Satguru Nanak. Kiu hatiai = how could one turn back? Meaning: O Guru Angad Sahib ji! You did not refuse to obey the order given by Guru Nanak.
(O Guru Angad Sahib ji!) Whatever order the Guru (Nanak Sahib) gave, you (accepted it) as true (and you) did not refuse to obey it;
The Guru gave the True Command; why should we hesitate to proclaim this?
The Guru uttered the truth regarding his successor. Why should we then desist from proclaiming this?
Whatever the Guru ordered is all true. Why should one turn back from carrying out the Guru's word? That is, O Lahna ji, you did not turn back; you kept obeying the command.
0747: Putri = by the sons. Kaul = word, order. Na palio = did not obey. Kannh = shoulders. Kar kannh = turning the shoulder, turning the face away, turning the back. Pirahu = from the Pir, from the Satguru. Murtiai = kept turning away.
The (Satguru's) sons did not obey his word; turning their backs on the Guru, they kept turning (the order) away.
His sons did not obey His Word; they turned their backs on Him as Guru.
The Guru's sons obeyed not his word and turned their back upon the proclaimed Guru.

And the sons, Baba Sri Chand Sahib and Lakhmi Chand Sahib, did not (na palio) obey the Guru's word. (Kar pirahu) They were to be made gurus of the world, but they (murtiai) turned their (kannh) shoulders — that is, Guru Nanak ji was displeased with them.
TE1Y: Dil khotai = because of a false heart. Aaki phirannh = (who) wander in revolt. Bannh = tying. Uchainnh = carry, bear. Bhar chhatiai = the load of a bundle. (Note: in 'phirannh', 'bannh' and 'uchainnh' the letter 'n' carries a half 'h'.)
Those who, because of a false heart, go about in revolt (against the Guru) carry around the tied-up bundle (of worldly affairs) as a load.
These evil-hearted ones became rebellious; they carry loads of sin on their backs.
The evil-hearted sons turned rebels and making a sack-Load of sins, carry it on their head.
The false-hearted sons went about in revolt against the Guru — that is, did not obey the Guru's command. They were carrying the (chhatiai) sack of the load of pride.
0SH7: Jin = the one (Guru Nanak) who. Aakhi = told (the teaching of obeying the order). Soi = (that Guru) himself. Kare = does (the work of walking in the order). Jin = the one (Guru Nanak) who. Kiti = made (this play of walking in the will). Tinai = he himself. Thatiai = shaped, established (Baba Lahna ji), made him able to obey the order.
The Guru Nanak who gave this order of accepting the will was himself the one who did the work; the one who made this (play of the order) himself made (Baba Lahna ji) able (to obey the order).
Whatever the Guru said, Lehna did, and so he was installed on the throne.
Whatever the Guru said, Lahna did the very same, was installed obeyed the order, was installed on the Guru's throne.

The Hari who (kiti) made the creation then took the form of Guru Nanak and (thatiai) established Guruship in the world. And the same Guru Nanak ji who said, "O Lahna! I have given you the Guruship" — that same Guru Nanak ji, in the form of Angad, is carrying out the Guruship.
D76L: Kaun hare = who lost (the game of walking in the order)? Kin = who? Uvatiai = won, earned, won the game, gained. Kaun hare kin uvatiai = who lost (in this play of the order) and who gained? Meaning: (by one's own power, in this play of the order) no one is a loser and no one is able to win. ||2||
(But what is in the power of beings? Relying on their own ability, in this play of the order) no one is a loser, and no one is able to win. ||2||
Who has lost, and who has won? ||2||
Lo, who has lost and who has won?
Hereafter people guess: let us see who will lose, and (kin uvatiai) who will win — that is, which of the sons and Sikhs will receive the Guruship next? ||2||
YAC8: Jin = the one (Guru Angad Dev ji) who. Kiti = did (the labour of obeying the Guru's order). Mannana = worthy of honour. Ko = who, who else? Sal = excellent, better. Jivahe = camel-thorn. {Camel-thorn grows in the riverbed lands where silt from the floods has raised the ground; it dries up in the rainy season, and, like pohli, it has thorns.} Sali = rice, which can thrive only in low ground.

The one (Guru Angad Dev ji) who (stayed humble and did the labour of obeying the Satguru's order) became worthy of honour. Which (of the two) is better — camel-thorn or rice? (Rice is better, which grows in low ground. In the same way, whoever stays low and obeys the order receives honour.)
He who did the work, is accepted as Guru; so which is better - the thistle or the rice?
He, who rendered service, is worshipped as the Guru. Which one is bitter, thistle or rice?
Knowing Guru Angad ji to be the very form of Guru Nanak ji, who gave him the Guruship, one should honour him; and some behaved (ko sal) falsely toward the Guru, and some (sali) excellently.
6VR5: Lai gala = hearing the words, hearing the pleas. Dalali = mediation.
Guru Angad Sahib has become the king of dharma, the god of dharma; hearing the pleas of beings, he is mediating to join them with Parmatma.
The Righteous Judge of Dharma considered the arguments and made the decision.
Weighing the merits of both the sides, the Guru, like the God, Righteous Judge, gave the reasonable decision.
Dharamrai, who is a god, will take their words and act as broker in between — that is, will give the fruit of their deeds.
SSEC: Sacha = Akal Purakh. Kare = brings into effect. Sa = that very. Darhali = at once, at that very moment.
(Now) whatever word the Satguru (Angad Dev) speaks, Akal Purakh does just that; that very thing comes about at once.
Whatever the True Guru says, the True Lord does; it comes to pass instantaneously.
Whatever the True Guru says, the True Lord does. That thing instantaneously comes to pass.
The one of whom the Satguru says, "He has behaved well toward us" — Dharamrai will make him true. Whatever the Guru says, that thing is to happen (darhali) at once, at that very moment.
4389: Dohi phiri = the fame of greatness spread. Kartai = by the Creator. Bandh = binding, making firm. Bahali = settled, established.
The fame of Guru Angad Dev (ji's) greatness has spread; the true Creator has made it firm and established it.
Guru Angad was proclaimed, and the True Creator confirmed it.
The sovereignty of Guru Angad was proclaimed and the True Creator confirmed it.
Now Sri Guru Angad ji's proclamation has gone round; (sach) surely Vahiguru has made it and (bahali) seated it.
7LAB: Kaia = body. Palat kar = changing. Mal takht = holding the seat. Sai dali = with hundreds of branches, with hundreds of Sikhs.

Guru Nanak, with hundreds of followers, changing the body (that is, in the form of Guru Angad Dev ji), sits holding the throne (within Guru Angad Dev ji is the very same light as Guru Nanak Sahib's; only the body has changed).
Nanak merely changed his body; He still sits on the throne, with hundreds of branches reaching out.
Changing his body, Nanak has occupied and sat on the throne, which has hundred of scions,
Sri Guru Nanak ji himself, changing the body, has taken the throne of Guruship — a throne with hundreds of branches, which are the Sikhs and the Sikhs of Sikhs.
XZ65: Umat = the sangat. Kharhi = standing, alert, with love. Dar seve = serves the door, stays at the door. Maskalai = with the burnisher. Hoe jangali = rusted metal (becomes clean).
The sangat serves with love (staying at Guru Angad Dev ji's) door (and is purifying its soul, as) rusted metal (becomes clean) with a burnisher.
Standing at His door, His followers serve Him; by this service, their rust is scraped off.
Standing at his door, his followers serve him, Thus is the rust of their sins scrubbed off.

At his door stand the (umat) Sikhs and servants. Their understanding, which had rusted with the rust of sin, found the burnisher of the Satguru's service. Maskala is the name of a particular stone with which weapons are polished.
BYFC: Dar = at (Guru Nanak's) door. Darves = one who asks for the gift of the Name. Khasamm dai nai sachai = through the Master's true Name, by the blessing of remembering the Master's true Name. Bani = has formed.
At (Guru Nanak's) door (Guru Angad) asks for the gift of the Name. By the blessing of remembering the true Name of Akal Purakh, a radiance has formed (on Guru Angad Sahib's face).
He is the Dervish - the Saint, at the door of His Lord and Master; He loves the True Name, and the Bani of the Guru's Word.
The Guru is the saint of the Lord's door and loves the True Name and the Guru's word.
You have become the Master's dervish; your Bani has formed (lali) a love for the true Name.
GD8J: Balvand = O Balvand! Khivi = (Mata) Khivi, wife of Guru Angad ji. Jis = whose (Mata Khivi ji's). Patrali = leafy, dense.

O Balvand! (Mata) Khivi ji (Guru Angad Dev ji's wife) is (also, like her husband) very good; Mata Khivi ji's shade is very leafy (dense) (that is, sitting near Mata Khivi ji too, peace and coolness arise in the heart).
Balwand says that Khivi, the Guru's wife, is a noble woman, who gives soothing, leafy shade to all.
Says Balwand, Guru Angad's consort, Khivi, is a good wife, who gives dense leafy shade of solace to all.
Rai Balvand says: Khivi is a (nek jan) good person. Khivi was the wife of Guru Angad ji. Her shade — of family, like leaves giving comfort — is great.
CJNR: Langar = in the langar. Amrit = the taste of the Name, which gives spiritual life. Ghiali = with ghee.

(As in Guru Angad Dev ji's langar, which is the sat sangat,) the wealth (of the Name) is handed out, the taste of the Name that gives spiritual life is handed out, (so, through Mata Khivi ji's service, in the langar) rice pudding rich with ghee is handed out (to all).
She distributes the bounty of the Guru's Langar; the kheer - the rice pudding and ghee, is like sweet ambrosia.
She distributes the Guru's wealth in his kitchen, Nectar-sweet rice-pudding mixed with clarified butter.

In the langar the Guru hands out wealth, money and cash; and there is rice pudding whose taste is like amrit, (ghiali) rich with ghee. Or: the inner langar runs — (amrit) wisdom, (ras) love, and the ghee-rich pudding of loving devotion; these things are received by Sikhs according to their fitness, as the Guru is, and other wealth too is handed out in the form of virtues such as detachment.
6C6L: Parali = the rice stalk from which the grain has been threshed; the stalk has turned yellow; yellow-faced, ashamed.
(Coming to Guru Angad Dev ji's door) the foreheads of the Guru's Sikhs are glowing, but the faces of those turned away from the Guru turn pale (with jealousy).
The faces of the Guru's Sikhs are radiant and bright; the self-willed manmukhs are pale, like straw.
Bright are the faces of the Guru's Sikhs and those of the perverse grow pale like straw.
The faces of the gurmukhs are bright in this world and the next; and the self-willed have become straw — that is, they stayed empty-handed from the Guru; human birth brought them no gain at all.
AL6B: Pae kabul = (Guru Angad Dev ji) was accepted. Khasamm nal = by his Satguru (Guru Nanak Dev ji). Mardi ghal = the labour of a true man.
When (Guru Angad Dev ji) did the labour of a true man, he was accepted at the door of his Satguru (Guru Nanak).
The Master gave His approval, when Angad exerted Himself heroically.
When Angad rendered manly service, then did his Master approve of him.
He was accepted as true by (khasamm) Vahiguru in the Court — (jan) the men who did the work; that is, Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji is that man.
1YHY: Sahu = husband. Soe = that. Jin = who. Goe = the earth. ||3||
That husband of Mata Khivi ji (Guru Angad Dev was such) that he had lifted up (the burden of the whole) earth. ||3||
Such is the Husband of mother Khivi; He sustains the world. ||3||
Such is mother Khivi's spouse, who sustains the whole world.
That is the husband of Mata Khivi ji who has lifted the whole (goe) game of the world — that is, he is the very form of the Formless. ||3||
KQBW: Horinon = from another direction. Vahaiai = has made flow, has set flowing. Duniai = the people of the world. Ki = what? Kion = he has done.
The world says (Guru Nanak) has made the Ganga flow from another direction. What is this he has done?
It is as if the Guru made the Ganges flow in the opposite direction, and the world wonders: what has he done?
Guru Nanak made the Ganges flow in another direction and people say, "What has he done?"
The whole (duniai) creation says that Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji has made the Ganga flow backwards: what is this he has done — leaving his sons and making a servant the master?
R35J: Isar = by the Lord, the Guru. Jagnath = by the Lord of the world. Uchahdi = high beyond limit. Vain = word. Virikion = he has spoken.
Guru Nanak, Lord of the world, has spoken a word that is high beyond all limit.
Nanak, the Lord, the Lord of the World, spoke the words out loud.
God incarnate Nanak, the Lord of the world, has uttered the supremely sublime hymns.
Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji is the all-powerful Master of the world, who (virikion) spoke words (uchahdi) higher than the limits of the world — that is, words about attaining the true form.
GYWZ: Parbat = Mount Sumer (meaning, a high awareness; as in the Puranic story the gods made Mount Sumer the churning-stick when churning the ocean of milk, so Guru Nanak made high awareness the churning-stick). Basak = Skt. vasuki, the king of snakes. Netr = in the churning rope. Kar netr basak = putting the serpent Basak into the churning rope (meaning, making the snake-like mind the churning rope — bringing the mind under control).

Making high awareness the churning-stick, and putting the (mind, like the) serpent Basak into the churning rope (that is, bringing the mind under control), he churned the 'Shabad' (that is, reflected on the 'Shabad'; in this way)
Making the mountain his churning stick, and the snake-king his churning string, He has churned the Word of the Shabad.
Making a mountain has churning staff and the Snake-King his churning-string, he has churned the Divine word.
He is the very form who made the mountain the churning-stick, put the serpent Basak as the churning rope, and churned the (sabad) ocean.
VHJB: Nikalian = he (Guru Nanak) brought out. Aavagaun = the world. Chilkion = he made it shine, made it bright, he (Guru Nanak) made it a place of peace.

He (Guru Nanak) brought out fourteen jewels (the 'divine virtues', from this ocean of the 'Shabad', as the gods brought fourteen jewels out of the ocean), and (by this effort) made the world beautiful.
From it, He extracted the fourteen jewels, and illuminated the world.
He has extracted the fourteen invaluable objects and has illumined the whole universe.

And bringing out the fourteen jewels, he (chilkion) made them shine in the (aavagaun) world. Or: Parmeshvar's grace was (1) the Mandrachal mountain, (2) the merit of beings the serpent Basak, (3) the Veda the ocean, (4) Guru Nanak ji as Vishnu, churning, brought out these 14 jewels, told next: devotion is Lakshmi (1), reflection on the self the gem (2), fame Rambha (3), love the wine (4), repeating the Name the amrit (5), singing raag the conch (6), firm faith the elephant (7), giving the moon (8), the sat sangat the wish-fulfilling tree (9), peace the wish-fulfilling cow (10), slander of the saints the poison (11), speaking truth the bow (12), the Satguru the royal physician Dhanvantari (13), wisdom the horse Uchaishrava (14). Sri Guru Nanak ji brought these inner jewels to light in the world.
R43P: Kudrat = power, ability. Ah = such. Vekhalian = he (Guru Nanak) showed. Jin = having won, (having won Baba Lahna ji's mind). Aivad = so great. Pid = body. Aivad pid = so high a soul. Thinkion = he sounded it, tapped it — as one taps a new pot to test it before buying — he, Guru Nanak, tested it.
He (Guru Nanak) showed such power that (first) winning (Baba Lahna ji's mind), he tested so high a soul,
He revealed such creative power, and touched such greatness.
He displayed such power when he assayed so great a person as Angad.
(Jin) He who has shown this power — on the support of his own being he has (thinkion) held in place (aivad pid) so great a body — that is, the universe.
W795: Lahne sir = on Lahna's head. Dharion = he placed. Asman = up to the sky. Kiarha = the neck. Chhikion = he stretched.
(then) he placed the canopy (of Guruship) on Baba Lahna ji's head, and raised (his) glory up to the sky.
He raised the royal canopy to wave over the head of Lehna, and raised His glory to the skies.
He waved the royal umbrella over the head of Lahna and extended the canopy of his glory to the sky.

He placed the canopy of Guruship on Lahna's head, and spread in the skies the (kiarha) canopy of praise. Or: Lahna ji's heart was a (kiarha) field, and the weed of pride that (as) was in it he (chhikion) pulled out — that is, by having him obey many kinds of impossible commands, he made his heart pure.
R3TG: Aap = himself. Aapai seti = with his own 'self'. Mikion = he (Guru Nanak) matched, made equal. {Note: when playing kabaddi and similar games, boys of equal strength and height first come 'matched' — two equal boys come forward and are picked for the two sides.}
(Guru Nanak Sahib's) soul so merged into (Baba Lahna ji's) soul that Guru Nanak made himself equal to his own 'self' (Baba Lahna ji).
His Light merged into the Light, and He blended Him into Himself.
Nanak's light merged in Guru Angad's light and the Guru Him self blended Angad with Himself.
The light merged into the light; Parmatma (mikion) joined himself with himself; or, his own here is himself. As water mixes with water, so light has merged into light.
94ZN: Ghokh kai = having tested {Note: where old Punjabi has 'kai', today we use 'ke'}. Umat = sangat. Ji = whatever. Kion = he (Guru Nanak) did.
O whole sangat! See what he (Guru Nanak) did, having tested his Sikhs and sons —
Guru Nanak tested His Sikhs and His sons, and everyone saw what happened.
Nanak tested his sikhs and his sons and all his sect saw what he had done.
The whole sangat says: see what the Guru did (ghokh kai) after weighing up the Sikhs and the sons.
ZLAT: Sudhos = he examined him, made trial of him. Tikion = he marked, he (Guru Nanak) chose. ||4||
when he made the test, he chose (Baba) Lahna (ji) (for his own place). ||4||
When Lehna alone was found to be pure, then He was set on the throne. ||4||
When Lahna was found immaculate, then alone the Guru established him on the throne.
When he (sudhos) examined and saw well that this was the fit one, he (tikion) seated Lahna ji as Guru — that is, established him on the seat of Guruship. ||4||
FKCJ: Khadur vasaia = increased the life of the town of Khadur. Pheruan satgur = by the Satguru, son of (Baba) Pheru.
Then (when Baba Lahna ji received the Guruship) the Satguru, son of Baba Pheru ji, brought new life to Khadur (that is, came from Kartarpur and settled in Khadur).
Then, the True Guru, the son of Pheru, came to dwell at Khadoor.
Then, the True Guru, the son of Pheru, came to abide in the village of Khadoor.

When, at a yogi's word, the landowners had lifted the Guru's bed and left it at the boundary of the village, Khadur began to be ruined by great famine and suffering. When they persuaded the Guru and brought him back, rain fell and the town was settled again; this is what is told here. The (pheruan) son of Pheru, Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji, settled Khadur again.
CJB6: Hor = the rest of the world. Much = very much. Garur = pride. Pher = after this.
(O Satguru!) The rest of the world takes great pride, but you, having repetition, austerity and self-discipline (with you, stayed as before in a humble nature).
Meditation, austerities and self-discipline rest with You, while the others are filled with excessive pride.
Meditation, hard service and self-discipline abide with you, O my Guru and excessive pride abides with others.
O Guru Angad Sahib ji! At all times there are with you repetition, austerity, mastery of the senses, dignity, and (much) many other virtues.
HRSH: As scum spoils water, so greed ruins people,
Greed ruins mankind, like the green algae in the water.
Avarice spoils the mortals, as the green moss does the water.
Greed is what destroys people. The example: as scum spoils water — that is, by being greedy we have met with such suffering.
XDY6: Varhiai = through the raining, through the rain. Kudrati = divine.
(but) because (the Name) rains down in the court of the Guru (Nanak), divine light (shines on you, O Guru Angad).
In the Guru's Court, the Divine Light shines in its creative power.
The Lord's Light spontaneously rains at the Guru's court.
O Guru ji! In your assembly the light of (kudrati) Parmeshvar rains down — that is, knowledge of the self is attained.
YSLE: Jit = in which. Hath = the bottom of the depth. Tharoor = cool water, a cool ocean.
You are that cool ocean whose depth cannot be found.
You are the cooling peace, whose depth cannot be found.
O my Guru, you are that peace, of which depth can be found not.
You have (tharoor) set down that very form — Parmeshvar, whose depth no one (labhai) finds; that is, He is endless.
YR7U: Nau nidh = the nine treasures. Nidhan = treasure. Bharpoor = brimful.
The treasure of the Prabhu's Name, which is (the world's) nine treasures, is brimful in your heart, (O Guru!)
You are overflowing with the nine treasures, and the treasure of the Naam, the Name of the Lord.
you are brimful with the nine treasure of the Name-wealth.
The treasure that is the nine treasures is brimming within you.
RFBQ: (O Guru Angad!) Whoever slanders you is ruined (by himself) (he brings spiritual death on himself).
Whoever slanders You will be totally ruined and destroyed.
He, who slanders you, is utterly ruined.
Whoever slanders you is crushed — that is, destroyed.
RDBN: Worldly beings see only what is close at hand (for the sake of the world they commit the sin of slander, not knowing its result; but, O Guru!) you see what will happen ahead too.
People of the world can see only what is near at hand, but You can see far beyond.
The people of this world are short-sighted, but you see afar.

Beings of the mortal world, such as us, have (nerhai disai) short sight, and (tudh sujhai door) you see far — that is, you have long sight, the vision of Brahm. Or: the mortal world — that is, death — seems near, meaning one takes oneself to be subject to death; on (sujhai) seeing your true form that goes far away — that is, the soul becomes sure of itself as imperishable.
X450: Then the Satguru (Angad Dev ji), son of Baba Pheru ji, brought good fortune to Khadur. ||5||
Then the True Guru, the son of Pheru, came to dwell at Khadoor. ||5||
Then the True Guru, the son of Pheru, came to abide in the village of Khadoor.
Guru Angad ji, son of Pheru! You came again and made Khadur flourish. ||5||

VBDF: Tika = the radiance of the forehead. Baihna = throne. Diban = court.
(On Guru Amar Das's forehead too) is the same radiance; (his too) is the same throne, the same court (as Guru Nanak's and Guru Angad Sahib's).
The same mark on the forehead, the same throne, and the same Royal Court.
Guru Amardas obtained the same apostolic mark, the same throne and the same court.
The same tilak of Guruship, the same throne, and the same court of Bhai Buddha and the others — that is, the assembly of Sikhs.
PMF9: Piyu jeviha = like the father (Guru Angad). Dade jeviha = like the grandfather (Guru Nanak). Parvan = accepted, worthy of honour.
The grandson-Guru (Guru Amar Das too) is an honoured (Guru) (because he too) is just like Guru Nanak and Guru Angad Sahib.
Just like the father and grandfather, the son is approved.
The grandson (Guru Amardas) is as acceptable as his father (Guru Angad) & grand father (Guru Nanak).
The father, Sri Guru Angad Dev ji; the grandfather, Sri Guru Nanak ji; like them, the grandson, Sri Guru Amar Das ji, is accepted.
C5M9: Jin = the one (grandson-Guru) who. Nehi = churning post. Basak = the crooked serpent-like mind. Tan = spiritual strength.
This Guru Amar Das too has made spiritual strength the churning post and put the (mind, like the) serpent into the churning rope,
He took the thousand-headed serpent as his churning string, and with the force of devotional love,
It is Guru Amardas, who through the force of Divine love, made the thousand-mouthed serpent his churning-Staff,
He has (ghatia) put Basak in place of the churning rope and made strength the churning post. The nehi is a fixed post of wood to which the churning-stick's rope is tied.
59MK: Virolia = churned. Mer = Mount Sumer, a high awareness.
made Mount Sumer (high awareness) the churning-stick, and churned the ocean (of the Guru's Shabad),
he churned the ocean of the world with his churning stick, the Sumayr mountain.
and who, making the Sumer mountain his churning-staff, churned the ocean of the world.
He who churned the ocean, making (mer) Mandrachal the churning-stick — in some age it is written as Sumer — that is, you are the form of Vishnu.
AJ0R: brought out fourteen jewels (the divine virtues, from that ocean of the Shabad), (with which) he brought light (the understanding of spiritual life, into the world).
He extracted the fourteen jewels, and brought forth the Divine Light.
He brought forth the fourteen gems and diffused and Divine Light all-round.
And bringing out the fourteen jewels, he made the jewels shine in the world — that is, you are that very Hari.
7TKM: Sahaj = the steady state. Jat = the power to hold the senses back from vices. Palan = saddle.
(Guru Amar Das) made the steady state his horse, and made the power to hold the senses back from vices its saddle;
He made intuition his horse, and chastity his saddle.
The divine knowledge he made his steed and chastity he made his caparison.
He has made wisdom the horse, and put continence on it as the saddle.
2PUV: Dhanakh = bow. Sat = pure conduct. Jas handa = of the praise (of Parmatma).
he strung the bow of pure conduct and (held) the arrow of Parmatma's praise.
He placed the arrow of the Lord's Praise in the bow of Truth.
On the bow of truth, he mounted the arrow of the Lord's praise.
And he has strung the bow of speaking truth, and made the uttering of praise the arrow.
X6YA: Kal = the world full of troubles. Dhoo andhar = pitch darkness. Rai = {raya} rays. Bhan = {bhanu} the sun.
In the world there was pitch darkness (of vices). (Guru Amar Das, as it were,) the sun with its rays rose,
In this Dark Age of Kali Yuga, there was only pitch darkness. Then, He rose like the sun to illuminate the darkness.
In the Darkage, there was pitch darkness. The Guru arose like the night-illuminating Sun.
In the Kali age there was great darkness. Your coming into it is as if the sun had risen, shining with its (rai) rays.
0UL9: Satahu = from 'sat', by the strength of pure conduct. Chhavan = shade, protection. Sa = was. Ban = arrow.
who by the strength of 'sat' alone made the (ruined) crop grow, and by 'sat' alone protected it.
He farms the field of Truth, and spreads out the canopy of Truth.
He has grown the field of truth, and has stretched and canopy of truth.

Being the very form of Guru Nanak ji, by your power you made grow again the field that the buffaloes had eaten, and by your power you held the shade of the tree in that same place. Or: you have grown the field of virtues such as truth, and stretched the (chhavan) canopy of the praise of Parmeshvar, whose form is Truth.
ZV6Y: (O Guru Amar Das!) In your langar too, ghee, fine flour and sugar (and other good things) are used every day.
Your kitchen always has ghee and flour to eat.
Ever in your kitchen are clarified butter and refined wheat flour to eat.
Every day in your kitchen there is ghee, fine flour and (khan) sugar — that is, karah prasad. Or: love, wisdom and devotion — this is your daily kitchen.
4N3V: The person who has settled your Shabad in his mind has come to understand (Parmatma, who dwells in) all four directions.
You understand the four corners of the universe; in your mind, the Word of the Shabad is approved and supreme.
You, O Amardas, Knowest the four quarters of the world and to your mind the Name is agreeable.
The one who has (parvan) firmly accepted your teaching in the mind sees the four directions as the form of Brahm.
0ALS: (O Guru!) The one to whom you have granted, through your glance of grace, the pass (of the Shabad) — you have ended his round of birth and death.
You eliminate the comings and goings of reincarnation, and bestow the insignia of Your Glance of Grace.
You obviously removest the coming and going of him, on whom you casteth your fovourable glance.
Those on whom you have cast your glance — you have openly ended their birth and death.
BPBY: Autaria = was born. Purakh sujan = the all-wise Akal Purakh.
That all-wise Akal Purakh has Himself come into the world, taking birth (in the form of Guru Amar Das).
You are the Avataar, the Incarnation of the all-knowing Primal Lord.
He, the wise Lord, descended in the form of Guru Amardas.
The all-wise Being, who is Parmeshvar — you are His incarnation, come down.
Q0Y6: Jhakharh = in a storm. Meran = Sumer.
(Guru Amar Das) does not waver in the storm (of vices); even if a gale (of vices) blows he does not waver; he is (as it were) Mount Sumer.
You are not pushed or shaken by the storm and the wind; you are like the Sumayr Mountain.
You are firm like the Sumer mountain and are swayed not by storm and gusts of wind.
You do not waver through (jhakharh) greed and (vau) desire; you are unmoving like Mount (meran) Sumer.
U6XB: Birtha jia ki = the pain of the heart.
He knows the pain in the hearts of beings; he is the knower of hearts.
You know the inner state of the soul; You are the Knower of knowers.
You, O Searcher of hearts, knowest the state of all mind.
Being the knower of hearts, you know the pain of all beings.
W19M: O King whose rule is ever-abiding! What praise can I give you? You are beautiful of soul and wise.
How can I praise You, O True Supreme King, when You are so wise and all-knowing?
How can I praise you, O True King, when you are Wise and Omniscient.
O True King! Since you yourself are the wisest of the wise, how can we praise you? That is, you are endless. The meaning is: without the heart's love, you are not pleased by outward praise.
AF6D: Dan = gift. Satgur bhavsi = pleases the Guru. So sate dan = to me, Satta, that gift of yours (is good).
To me, Satta, that gift of yours is good which pleases (you,) the Satguru.
Those blessings granted by the Pleasure of the True Guru - please bless Satta with those gifts.
The bounties which you, O True Guru, likest to grant; bless you Satta with those gifts.
O Satguru! The gift that pleases you — that is, the Name of God, which pleases you — give it to me, Satta.
CQAU: Handa = of. Sir = on the head. Umat = the sangat.
(Seeing) Guru Nanak's canopy on the head (of Guru Amar Das ji), the sangat is amazed.
Seeing Nanak's canopy waving over Your head, everyone was astonished.
Seeing Nanak's umbrella, wavering over your head, the entire sect is astonished.
Seeing that the canopy which was on Sri Guru Nanak ji's head is on your head, the sangat is amazed.
K6W3: (On his forehead too) is the same radiance; (his too) is the same throne, the same court (as Guru Nanak's and Guru Angad Sahib's).
The same mark on the forehead, the same throne, and the same Royal Court.
Guru Amardas has the Same mark, the same throne and the same court.
The same tilak of Guruship, the same throne, and the same court of Bhai Buddha and the others — that is, the assembly of Sikhs.
7J2Z: The grandson-Guru (Guru Amar Das too) is an honoured Guru (because he too) is just like Guru Nanak and Guru Angad Sahib. ||6||
Just like the father and grandfather, the son is approved. ||6||
The grandson is as acceptable as his father and grandfather (Guru Nanak.).
The father, Sri Guru Angad Dev ji; the grandfather, Sri Guru Nanak ji; like them, the grandson, Sri Guru Amar Das ji, is accepted. ||6||
YLSG: Jin = the one (the Prabhu) who. Siria = created.
Blessed, blessed is Guru Ram Das! The Akal Purakh who created (Guru Ram Das) also made him beautiful.
Blessed, blessed is Guru Raam Daas; He who created You, has also exalted You.
Blessed, blessed is Guru Ramdas. The Lord, who created you; He alone has embellished you.
Blessed in mind and speech, O Sri Guru Ram Das ji! The Parmeshvar who created you has also adorned you by giving you the Guruship.
L3A7: It is a complete miracle that the Creator has Himself (placed Himself in him).
Perfect is Your miracle; the Creator Lord Himself has installed You on the throne.
Complete is your miracle. The Creator Himself has installed you on the throne.
That the miracle has come to you in full — the Creator, who is Parmeshvar, has Himself taken your form.
5NLL: Sikhi = by the Sikhs. Atai = and.
All the Sikhs and sangats have bowed to him, knowing him as the form of Akal Purakh.
The Sikhs and all the Congregation recognize You as the Supreme Lord God, and bow down to You.
Deeming you as the Transcendent Lord, yours followers and congregation bow before you.
The Sikhs who stay near, and the sangats too, have bowed, knowing you as Parbrahm.
DRX1: Athah = whose depth cannot be found, very deep. Paravaria = the far and near shores.

(O Guru Ram Das!) You are ever-abiding; you cannot be weighed (that is, your virtues cannot be counted; you are an ocean whose) depth cannot be found, and the end of whose far and near shores cannot be reached.
You are unchanging, unfathomable and immeasurable; You have no end or limitation.
You are Unshakable, Unfathomable and Unweighable. You have no end or bounds.
Unshakeable, fathomless and beyond weighing is your form; there is no end to your far and near shores.
0F6D: The people who have lovingly obeyed your order — you have carried them across (the world-ocean).
Those who serve You with love - You carry them across.
They, who serve you with love Then you ferrieest across.
The devotees who have served you with love — you have carried those devotees across the world.
KSF8: Tudh = you. Saparvaria = together with (the rest of the vices, their) family.
From within them you have killed and driven out greed, avarice, lust, anger, attachment and all the other vices.
Greed, envy, sexual desire, anger and emotional attachment - You have beaten them and driven them out.
You have beaten and driven out avarice, covetousness, sexual desire, wrath and worldly love with all their ramifications.
Greed, avarice, lust, anger, attachment — you have killed and driven them all out of the inner self, together with their family.
JGFR: Paiskaria = the display, the festivity made to welcome a great person on arrival; the expanse of the sangat.
(O Guru Ram Das!) I am a sacrifice to the place where you dwell. Your sangat is forever unshakeable.
Blessed is Your place, and True is Your magnificent glory.
Praiseworthy is Your place and true are yours bounties.
Your place, the sat sangat, is worthy of praise, and your expanse of devotion is true too. Or: (paiskar) your servants, all together, are true too.
VKTE: (O Guru Ram Das ji!) You yourself are Guru Nanak, you yourself are Baba Lahna; I have understood you to be Guru Amar Das.
You are Nanak, You are Angad, and You are Amar Daas; so do I recognize You.
You are Nanak, you are Angad and you are Guru Amardas. So do I deem you.
You are Sri Guru Nanak ji, and you are Lahna ji too; and I have understood you to be Guru Amar Das ji as well.
AZ1J: Sadharia = came to rest. Too = you. ||7||
(Whoever) has had the vision of the Guru (Ram Das) — his mind then came to rest. ||7||
When I saw the Guru, then my mind was comforted and consoled. ||7||
When I saw the Guru, then was my soul sustained.
O Sri Guru Ram Das ji! Those who have seen your form have (sadharia) purified their mind, or given it a support. ||7||
68E1: Chare = all four (earlier Gurus). Chahu jugi = in their four bodies. Jage = became manifest, shone forth. Panchain = (panch ayan, the home of the five, the source of the five elements) Akal Purakh (as in: "Manak man meh man marsi, sach na lagai kat. Raja takht tikai guni, bhai panchain rat" — Maru Mehla 1, ang 992; and "Taskar mar vasi panchain, adal kare vichare. Nanak Ram nam nistara gurmat milah piare" — Suhi Chhant M1, Ghar 3). Bhai panchain = in the fear of Panchain, in the fear of Parmatma. Panchain = in Panchain, in Parmatma.
All four Gurus shone forth, each in his own time; Akal Purakh Himself became manifest (in them).
The four Gurus enlightened the four ages; the Lord Himself assumed the fifth form.
The four Gurus illumined their own four times. You, O Nanak, yourself have assumed the fifth form.

In the world, in (chahu jugi) four ages, the four Gurus, as incarnations, (jage) became manifest — from Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji at the beginning through Sri Guru Ram Das ji. O Guru Arjan Sahib ji! You yourself have become⁽¹⁾ the fifth incarnation.
FDSF: Aapinnhai = by Himself, the Prabhu Himself. Aap = Himself. Sajion = He made manifest (in the form of the creation). Thammh = supporting, holding up.
Akal Purakh Himself made Himself manifest (in the form of the creation), and He Himself (in the form of the Guru) is holding up the creation.
He created Himself, and He Himself is the supporting pillar.
You Yourself didst create the world and yourself are its ever standing pillar.
By Himself He made the world, His own form, and then He Himself, as its support, stands holding the world in place.
MWTF: Likhanhara = the writer, the one who draws the guidelines.
(To guide beings, to draw their guidelines,) the Prabhu Himself is the tablet, He Himself the pen, and He Himself (in the form of the Guru) is the one who writes the guidelines.
He Himself is the paper, He Himself is the pen, and He Himself is the writer.
You yourself are the tablet, yourself the pen and yourself have become the writer.
He Himself is the tablet, which is the forehead; He Himself the pen, which is the command; He Himself, in the form of Brahma, has become the writer of destinies.
13QL: Umat = the creation. Niroa = free of disease.
The whole creation is in the round of birth and death, but the Prabhu Himself is (always) new and free of disease (that is, He is in every new colour and yet untouched).
All His followers come and go; He alone is fresh and new.
Yours followers are all subject to coming and going. You are ever safe and sound.
The whole creation comes and goes, and You, Parmeshvar, are Yourself ever new and (niroa) healthy — that is, free of disease.
9B0W: Takht = on the throne. Khivai = shines (Skt. kshibh, to shine).

On the throne (granted by that ever-new, healthy Prabhu, on which the first four Gurus shone, each in his own time, now) Guru Arjan is seated; the Satguru's canopy is shining (that is, the radiance and glory of Satguru Arjan Sahib is spreading everywhere).
Guru Arjun sits on the throne; the royal canopy waves over the True Guru.
Guru Arjan is seated on Guru Nanak's throne and the True Guru's canopy shines over him.
O Guru Arjan Sahib ji! Now you yourself sit on the throne, and your canopy of praise (khivai) is shining.
G1FV: Tai = and. Ugvanahu = from sunrise. Athvanahu = from sunset. Chahu chaki = in the four directions. Kian = he has made. Loa = light.
From sunrise (to sunset) and from sunset (to sunrise), he (Guru Arjan) has spread light in all four directions.
From east to west, He illuminates the four directions.
From east to west, you have illumined the four directions.
From (ugvanahu) the east (tai) and (athvanahu) the west, in all four directions, he has spread the light of his glory.
BC08: Moa = death, plague {note: the reading here is 'moa', but the actual word is 'mua'}.
The self-willed people who did not obey the Guru's order were struck by the plague (that is, they died spiritually).
Those self-willed manmukhs who do not serve the Guru die in shame.
The apostates, who serve not their Guru, die an ignoble death.
O Satguru ji! The self-willed who have not served you — death is dear to those self-willed ones; that is, they have fallen into birth and death.
2D61: Karamat = greatness, glory, miracle. Dhoa = gift, present. Chauni = fourfold.
Guru Arjan's greatness grows twofold (by day) and fourfold (by night); the Guru is the true gift of the true Prabhu (to the creation).
Your miracles increase two-fold, even four-fold; this is the True Lord's true blessing.
This is the True Guru's true blessing on you that yours miracles increase two-fold and four-fold.

O Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji! In you is miracle twofold and fourfold — that is, more and more; or the miracle of the six Shastras — that is, the strength of the conclusions of all the Shastras. And, O true Satguru, your (dhoa) union is forever.
C016: All four Gurus shone forth, each in his own time; Akal Purakh became manifest (in them). ||8||1||
The four Gurus enlightened the four ages; the Lord Himself assumed the fifth form. ||8||1||
The four Guru's illumined their own four times, You, O Nanak, yourself has assumed the filth form.

'Chare jage chahu jugi panchain aape hoa': in the world (chahu jugi), the four Gurus as incarnations became manifest; O Guru Arjan ji, you yourself have become the fifth incarnation. ||8||1|| ☬ As soon as they uttered this Bani of praise, their leprosy was cured. ☬ A yogi came to Kabir ji and said: "Drink wine, and you will have the bliss of samadhi."
